author: kirubaharan181
description: Use when assessing a pull request for correctness, design, standards, merge readiness. Do NOT use for writing code.
purpose: Provides independent review of changes before merge: pull request quality, peer review, architecture conformance, static analysis, dependency and coverage review, standards validation and technical debt. It owns stages 68-76 and keeps reviewers independent of authors.
when_to_use: A pull request needs review before merge.
Static analysis, dependency or coverage results need interpreting.
A change must be checked against agreed architecture or standards.
when_not_to_use: Running the test suites: use quality-assurance.
prerequisites: A pull request or diff with tests and a description.
Coding standards and tool configuration (see engineering-governance).
Reviewer who is not the author.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: review findings split into blockers and suggestions

decision_rules.situation: Tool configuration weakened in the same change

decision_rules.action: Ask for tests or a recorded decision.

decision_rules.situation: Author and reviewer are the same
decision_rules.action: Reject the review; request an independent one.

quality_gates: All tools ran on the change
Findings cite file, rule and reason

examples.title: Review a pull request
examples.request: Review PR 482 which adds refund handling.
examples.context: Diff touches payments and orders; tests included.
examples.behavior: Run tool checks, read the diff for error handling and authorization, check coverage on changed lines, and list blockers separately.
examples.output: Review with one blocker (no ownership check) and two suggestions.
examples.acceptance: Blocker has a file reference and a fix suggestion.

examples.title: Judge a suppression
examples.request: The change adds two lint suppressions.
examples.context: One has a ticket; one hides an unused variable.
examples.behavior: Accept the documented one, reject the other and ask for removal.
examples.output: Findings with the decision for each.
examples.acceptance: Each added suppression has a recorded decision.

limitations: Cannot find defects in code it was not shown or tests that were not run.
Does not approve merge by itself: a named human reviewer approves where required.
Static analysis gives false positives and negatives.

troubleshooting.resolution: State that review is incomplete and ask for the results.
Ask the author to split it.
Escalate to the engineering lead and record the decision.
